name: session-mgmt
description: Manage the full lifecycle of a Claude Code working session. start-session opens a task in a fresh, isolated git worktree (via EnterWorktree, never `git worktree add`) named after the argument on branch `worktree-<name>`, reports what untracked state the worktree inherited — `.worktreeinclude` copies, symlinked node_modules — and whether its `.env` still points at the main checkout's stack, and loads the JIRA story when the name is an issue key. exit-session tears down the ephemeral resources a session created — background processes and dev servers, Docker/compose stacks, local Kubernetes, git worktrees (unlocking them first), throwaway local branches, and temp files — permission-free, then quits the CLI. Runs prompt-free in default, accept-edits and auto mode; a bundled UserPromptSubmit hook refuses only plan mode, where mutating tools are off. It hands back the deny-listed remote/history ops rather than running them.
